adjudication.resolution: The document genuinely prints the qualifier the queue flags: page 1 body prose (index 4) states, 'The withholding allowance amounts in Table 4 apply only to employees whose most recent withholding certificate was filed prior to 2020.' Prose index 3 identifies the table as 'Table 4. Withholding allowance by payroll period', i.e. grid p1_t3, whose rows run Weekly through Annually — so the restriction qualifies all six withholding_allowance records, not any single row. The pipeline's reading is therefore accurate: this is a real, table-wide document fact, not a misread. The closed extra-attr dictionary for withholding_allowance defines only payroll_period, periods_per_year and allowance; none carries an applicability/eligibility restriction, and under the closed-dictionary rule an invented key (e.g. some 'applies_only_if_certificate_pre_2020' spelling) may not be used, since nothing downstream would read it. The correct disposition is: leave the Table 4 cell mappings as read (each period row yields its periods_per_year figure and its allowance amount exactly as printed), do NOT force the restriction into an extra attr or drop it, and keep the open issue naming the vocabulary gap — withholding_allowance has no listed key for this applicability condition — so the limitation remains visible. Either way the records land (accepted or not), the facts stand: the allowance figures map correctly, and the pre-2020-certificate restriction exists in the document with no home in the current schema.

The document does print this rule verbatim: prose block 4 on page 1 reads 'Employers must begin withholding in the pay period in which cumulative wages for the calendar year exceed $200,000, without regard to the employee's filing status or to wages paid by another employer.' The flag is therefore a genuine coverage question, not a misread of the page. The printed trigger is factually distinct from the Table 3 surtax liability thresholds: Table 3 shows $250,000 for married filing jointly and $125,000 for married filing separately against the flat $200,000 withholding start, so the prose figure is not a restatement of any single table cell, and silently dropping it would lose information (an MFJ employee's employer begins withholding before that employee's stated liability threshold). Judged against the closed record-type list and the closed extra-attr dictionary, the document fact has no home: no record type covers a standalone employer withholding trigger, the additional_medicare surtax_threshold slots are already occupied by the per-filing-status Table 3 thresholds and the employer_match false statement from the same paragraph, and no listed extra attr exists for a withholding-start threshold. The correct disposition is to CLOSE this item as a confirmed schema gap, not as a data error: forcing the prose into an invented key, or duplicating a bare additional_medicare threshold of 200000 onto the surtax set without a filing status, would violate the closed-vocabulary and no-duplicate rules. The reviewer should (a) confirm no surrogate record was nevertheless produced for this fact — i.e., no additional_medicare surtax_threshold record lacking a filing-status column alongside the legitimate single/head-of-household $200,000 rows, and no repurposed wage_base or employment_tax_rate record carrying it — and (b) file an issue naming the missing vocabulary entry so the fact can be carried under a defined key once the dictionary is extended. Until then, the faithful state of the extraction is that this employer-trigger sentence is intentionally unmapped.
